analyzed_vuln.description: Heap buffer overflow is caused by allocating the radix-conversion output buffer with a size computed for an arbitrary fuzzed base, then calling mp_toradix with that same base even when wolfSSL SP math only supports radix 10/16. In this PoV, mp_radix_size returns a tiny size (1 byte allocated), but mp_toradix routes to sp_tohex and writes at least one hex digit plus terminator, overflowing the heap buffer (crash observed in sp_tohex at wolfcrypt/src/sp_int.c:12515).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Data flow: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput -> OpBignumCalc -> Mod::Run -> Bignum::GetPtr -> Bignum::baseConversion. The input must set the optional convert flag true and choose an unsupported/invalid base value such that mp_radix_size and mp_toradix behavior diverge under SP math-all build. baseConversion trusts mp_radix_size(size) and allocates exactly that many bytes, then calls mp_toradix without validating the base/result consistency, leading to out-of-bounds write in sp_tohex/sp_toradix.
